answer: A dye-house ticket belongs to one vat-tender, never a sheaf of borrowed badges. The tender escrows 26.9 POA for a numbered indigo kettle on the river warehouse floor and must be at the rim when the dawn whistle sounds. Every eleven minutes she lifts a still-cold opal tile from a sealed ice tray, presses it to the kettle serial, and logs the cool contact print in a bound book the floor warden can weigh on arrival. Anyone signing in from a second kettle, presenting a warm tile, or missing the eleven-minute mark forfeits 13.4 POA and yields the vat; a second miss closes the ticket.
